question: A patient stung by approximately 500 bees who develops haemolysis, acute kidney injury, and hepatitis is experiencing an IgE-mediated anaphylactic reaction requiring adrenaline as the primary treatment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: FALSE. Mass envenomation (>50–100 stings) is DIRECT TOXIC injury (melittin-driven haemolysis and organ damage) — NOT anaphylaxis. Treatment is aggressive IV fluids, urine alkalinisation, and supportive care. Adrenaline is the treatment for ANAPHYLAXIS (sensitised patient, typically single sting). Distinguishing these two syndromes is essential.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Mass bee envenomation (typically >50–100 stings) causes DIRECT TOXICITY from the cumulative dose of melittin and phospholipase A2 — it is NOT IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. The mechanism is direct lysis of red cells and organ injury, producing haemolysis, rhabdomyolysis, AKI, and hepatitis. Treatment is supportive (fluids, urine alkalinisation, renal protection) — NOT adrenaline. Adrenaline is for anaphylaxis (single-sting in sensitised patient).
